title: Applied ML: Regression Triage for Prompt Sets, Quantization, and Model Onboarding
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Summary:
This playbook describes the standard process for detecting, triaging, and remediating regressions that originate from prompt set changes, quantization profile updates, or model onboarding events. It is intended for Applied ML engineers, SRE, and partner owners who operate the eval-harness and maintain production prompt sets and quantization profiles.

Scope:
- Prompt-set updates (new prompts, edits to existing prompts, re-labelling)
- Quantization profile changes (8-bit/4-bit conversions, kernel/runtime flags)
- Model onboarding and model variant swaps (e.g., v1 -> v2, fp16 -> quantized)
- Regressions detected by automated eval-harness runs, monitoring alerts, customer reports, or CI gating failures

Owners and Roles:
- Primary: Applied ML (owner: Aisha Patel)
- On-call SRE: responsible for alert routing and initial incident cadence
- Model Owner: person/team that onboarded the model or owns the prompt set
- QA / Product Safety: verify any behavioral/guardrail regressions
- Customer Success: liaison for customer-impacting regressions

Definitions and Severity Levels:
1) Severity P1 (production impacting):
   - Observable customer-facing correctness or safety regressions on critical flows
   - Delta in key eval metrics (e.g., task accuracy, hallucination rate) >= 10% relative degradation vs baseline for top-10 prompts
   - Immediate remediation required (rollback or hotfix)
2) Severity P2 (degradation):
   - Moderate drop in metrics (5-10% relative) or narrow-case functional regressions affecting fewer users
   - Prioritize next-day remediation and targeted debugging
3) Severity P3 (regression candidate):
   - Small metric changes (<5%) or non-critical edge-case behavior change
   - Track and schedule follow-up during normal sprint cadence

Detection Sources (examples):
- Scheduled eval-harness nightly and canary runs (baseline vs candidate comparisons)
- CI gating on PRs (model onboarding, quantization config changes)
- Observability: regression alerts from eval-metrics-diff pipeline, anomaly detection on latency/cost/quality signals
- Customer reports or support tickets flagged by Customer Success

Automated Triage Checklist (first 15-30 min):
1) Confirm alert and severity: gather alert context (metric, prompt IDs, model version, time window).
2) Reproduce locally: run the eval-harness with the same seed, prompt-set subset, and model artifact.
   - Command example: 
     eval-harness run --model-path s3://models/team/model:v2 --prompt-set prompts/top-50.json --seed 42 --metrics accuracy,fluency,hallucination --output /tmp/regression-run.json
3) Compare against baseline: generate a differential report (diff percent +/-).
   - Pass threshold check: 
     - If accuracy drop >= 10% on any priority prompt OR hallucination increase >= 10% -> P1
4) Identify change vector: was the recent change a prompt edit, quantization push, or model swap? Use Git history, deployment notes, and release notes.

Isolation Matrix (quick decisions):
- If change = quantization profile update and regression present -> immediately run the model with prior fp16/previous quantization profile. If prior profile passes, prepare rollback of quantization (see rollback steps).
- If change = prompt-set edit -> revert recent prompt edits in staging and re-run eval-harness on the reduced set.
- If change = model onboarding -> test the previous model artifact pinned in production; if previous model restores behavior, consider immediate rollback of rollout/A-B traffic.

Rollback and Mitigation Procedures:
A) Quantization rollback (recommended for P1/P2 with clear quantization correlation):
   1) Pin model to previous quantized artifact (if an artifact-level regression) OR disable quantization flag in deployment (if runtime flag caused issue).
   2) Deploy rollback to canary (5% traffic) and run end-to-end smoke tests + subset of prompt set.
   3) If smoke tests pass, promote rollback to 100% following standard deployment cadence.
   4) Post-deploy: run full nightly eval-harness and mark regression incident for RCA.

B) Prompt-set revert:
   1) Checkout prompt-set repo at previous commit: 
      git checkout refs/heads/main~1 -- prompt-sets/top-50.json
   2) Re-run eval-harness against candidate model to confirm restoration.
   3) If restored, publish emergency prompt-set revert and notify product/UX owner.

C) Model rollback / traffic reweighting:
   1) Using rollout controller, reweight traffic to previous model variant (example: reweight current 70/30 -> 0/100 to previous artifact).
   2) Validate with smoke & canary tests.

Assessment and Root Cause Determination (24-72 hours):
1) Correlate: cross-reference eval-harness diffs, model artifacts (hashes), quantization profiles, and deployment timestamps.
2) Re-run microbenchmarks: sequence-length edge cases, prompt-prefix sensitivity tests, and KV cache behavior on serving runtime.
3) Investigate hardware/kernel differences: check kernel selection logs for quantized kernels or fallback slow paths.
4) If a quantization bug is suspected, add a focused test in quantization-profiles CI that reproduces the failure.

Metrics and Alerting Thresholds (recommended):
- Nightly eval-harness diff alert when: relative delta >= 5% for any top-10 prompt OR mean metric shift >= 3% across prompt-set
- Safety/hallucination alerts: absolute increase in hallucination rate > 2 percentage points AND relative > 25%
- Latency regression alert: p95 latency increase > 20% and absolute > 300ms

Communication and Coordination:
- Immediate: open incident in PagerDuty and post summary to #applied-ml-incidents with title, severity, suspected cause, and immediate action.
- Stakeholders to notify: Product Safety, Customer Success (if customers affected), SRE, and Model Owner.
- Use communication template: 
  "Summary: [one-line] - Impact: [users/flows] - Action: [rollback/deploy/monitor] - Owner: [name]"

Postmortem and RCA Expectations:
- For any P1 incident: write a postmortem within 72 hours, include timeline, detection source, actions taken, root cause, and action items with owners and ETA.
- Add new regression test(s) to eval-harness and CI that prevent the same regression vector.
- If regression was caused by quantization, add a quantization-profile test matrix to cover failing prompts/behaviors.

Playbook Appendix (examples and snippets)
1) eval-harness differential run example:
   - JSON output diff command: 
     jq -S . /tmp/regression-run.json > /tmp/regression-sorted.json
     python tools/diff_report.py --baseline s3://eval-baselines/model:v1/top-50.json --candidate /tmp/regression-sorted.json --out /tmp/diff-report.html
2) Example quantization-profile quick table (human-readable):
   | profile_name | bits | per_channel | backend | notes |
   | QP-8-default  | 8    | true        | x86-cu | baseline 8-bit profile used in canary |
   | QP-4-aggressive | 4  | false       | cu-accel | high compression; known to reduce fluency on long-context prompts |
3) Prompt-set YAML fragment (example):
   - id: "invoice-extraction-01"
     priority: high
     description: "extract invoice amount and vendor name"
     examples: |
       - Input: "Invoice: ACME Corp, Amount: $3,450"
         Expected: {"vendor":"ACME Corp","amount":3450}

4) Quick checklist to add new regression tests to CI:
   - Add a new prompt to prompt-sets/regression-cases.yaml with 'regression_guard: true'
   - Create an eval-harness test case entry referencing the prompt id
   - Add a quantization matrix job on PRs that runs candidate quantization profiles for the model
